fig1_speed_distribution.svg: Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution $f(v)$ for N$_2$ at 300 K, from maxwell_speed_pdf. The three characteristic speeds (dashed) sit in the temperature-independent order $v_p<\langle v\rangle<v_\mathrm{rms}$ = $1:\sqrt{4/\pi}:\sqrt{3/2}$ (422 < 476 < 517 m/s): the peak, the mean, and the root-mean-square speed.
fig2_temperature_dependence.svg: The same distribution (N$_2$) at 200, 500 and 1000 K from maxwell_speed_pdf. Heating pushes the most-probable speed out as $v_p\propto\sqrt{T}$ (dotted) and flattens the curve, yet each integrates to 1 ($\int f\,dv\approx1$): a hotter gas spreads the same total probability over a wider, faster band of speeds.
